description:
pkix-lint/src/lib.rs:1107 and 1186:

    #[cfg(feature = \"oscal\")]
    pub fn filter_to_ids(self, ids: &[String]) -> Result<LintRunner, ...>

    #[cfg(feature = \"oscal\")]
    pub fn apply_parameter_overrides(
        &mut self,
        overrides: &[crate::oscal::profile::ParameterOverride],
    ) -> Result<(), crate::oscal::parse::ParseError>

These are the only ways to:
  - filter a LintRunner to a subset of lint IDs after construction
  - update lint parameters on an existing LintRunner

Both are gated behind the `oscal` cargo feature. Without that feature
enabled, a caller has zero post-construction mutation surface on
LintRunner. The signatures of run_cert and the rest of the runner
don't change with the feature.

This forces:

  - Callers who don't use OSCAL but DO want to filter or re-parameterize
    have to either enable the feature (pulling in serde_json) or rebuild
    the LintRunner from scratch each time their config changes.

  - The 'lint set composition' workflow is implicitly tied to OSCAL.
    Per AGENTS.md non-negotiable #5, OSCAL is 'one supported wire
    format', not the canonical one. But programmatically, OSCAL is
    the only first-class composition path.

# What's leaking

The `ParameterOverride` type lives in the oscal module. Its semantics
are general (composite param_id + value), not OSCAL-specific. But the
method that consumes it is gated, and there's no oscal-feature-free
analogue:

    // What's missing:
    pub fn set_parameter(&mut self, lint_id: &str, param_id: &str, value: &str)
        -> Result<(), ParameterError>;

A method on LintRunner that directly delegates to
`lint.set_parameter(...)` for the lint matching `lint_id` would give
parameter tuning without requiring OSCAL plumbing.

Same for filter_to_ids: it could trivially exist as a non-oscal-gated
method taking `&[&str]` or `&[impl AsRef<str>]`, with the OSCAL
adapter being a thin wrapper that calls it with the catalog ids.

# Forward fit

This is structural: the engine has the capability but the gating
hides it from non-OSCAL consumers. Pre-1.0 fix: introduce non-oscal
methods on LintRunner that do the actual work (`set_parameter`,
`filter_to_ids` with `&[&str]`), then have the OSCAL-feature variants
of these methods that take OSCAL types call into them.

# Why P2

Mitigations exist (rebuild the runner; enable the feature). The
gating is intentional and the OSCAL framing was the recent change.
But the contract still says 'parameter tuning is for OSCAL users' which
is not the workspace stance.
title: API contract: LintRunner exposes apply_parameter_overrides only under oscal feature, locking parameter tuning to OSCAL
